value: MWCC GC 1.2.5, -O4,p. v3 MERGES claim.law.NM_branch-pair-fusion-is-blocked-by-a-return-not-by-a-goto.20260903.v2 with claim.law.BF_the-unfused-branch-pair-is-an-inlined-callee-return-not-any-return.20260903.v1, whose discriminators DISAGREED: v2 says a `return` then-block is never folded, BF measured a function-scope `return` folding three ways. BF's is the correct one and v2's is the special case. Authored by the run-46 TOOL lane from both lanes' records plus the zero-build measurements marked NEW below; no new closure is claimed here. PART 1 -- THE SCREEN, unchanged. The target's recurring `b<cond> <next+4>` + unconditional `b <exit>` pair (fndiff --ops: `target-only: +1 b +1 bge/ble/bne  ours-only: -1 blt/bgt/beq`) is neither a peephole artifact nor source-unreachable: our own objects emit it at 503 sites across 257 objects (census at ca4074cb1; retail carries 563). A then-block that is a `goto <label>` IS folded to a single inverted conditional and NO spelling of the goto escapes it -- measured folds, all NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL or worse: `if (c) goto A; goto B;` (InitTexMods, DoAudioTallySFX, PlaceItem, ControllerMessageBox), `if (c) goto A; else goto B;`, an if/else diamond with an EMPTY then-arm, and `do { if (c) break; ... } while (0)`. DO NOT reach for `#pragma peephole off`: on InitTexMods it regressed real 2 -> 18 and STILL emitted the fused `blt`. PART 2 -- THE DISCRIMINATOR (BF's refinement; this REPLACES v2's 'a return is never folded'). What keeps the pair unfused is that the branch is created when a HELPER'S `return` is INLINED at a merge point inside the caller: the pair is emitted after the fold peephole has run, so nothing inverts it. A `return` written at FUNCTION scope, branching to the function's own epilogue, DOES fold. Measured on game/sound/sounds AudioSetupLevelStreams, where the target holds `cmpwi r0,3; ble ->60; b ->2f8` and 0x2f8 IS the epilogue (lmw r28,40(r1) / lwz r0,60(r1) / addi r1,r1,56 / mtlr r0 / blr): three distinct spellings all produced our single folded `bgt ->2f8`, every one NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL against the same object bytes -- (a) `if (sMusicSubState < 2 && sCurMusicVol > 3) { return; }`, (b) the same split into nested `if`s each with its own `return`, (c) `if (A) goto vol_ok; if (B) goto vol_ok; return; vol_ok:;`. v2's three `if (A || B) { return; }` closures (DoAudioTallySFX real 5 -> 0, InitTexMods 2 -> 0, DoPolyInst 4 -> 0) are NOT counter-examples: in each the guarded region is itself the inlined shape, which is why v2's rule appeared to hold. PART 3 -- THE CURE, and how to recognise the site before spending a probe. Lift the guarded region into a helper defined BEFORE its caller and let MWCC inline it, writing the early exit as `return`; leave the outer function a single `return <call>` or a single assignment from it. In the ALIGNED view (`fnasm.py <unit> <fn> --diff`, never two absolute offsets) the tell is: the pair's unconditional `b` lands on a block that ASSIGNS a value and falls through to the consumer (`li rN,0`, `mr rN,rM`, `lha rN,<disp>(rB)`), and other exits of the same region branch to that same block. That block IS the inline-return join and rN is the inline's result register. Confirming evidence is often in the same object: FindWorldObject, already at real 0, contains a second INLINED copy of FindWORLDOBJ's walk and carries the identical unfused pair at its inline-return site (+0x64 `bne ->6c` / `b ->cc`). CLOSURES across both lanes: FindWORLDOBJ real 17 -> 0, AudioEnterNextStage 4 -> 0, CritterMoveSetup 7 -> 0 (helper CritterMoveColNode, `if (nodeIndex < 0) return node;`), adsMoveRawToCooked 74 -> 0 BYTE-EXACT (two helpers), cardThreadMain 43 -> 20 with COUNT PARITY GAINED and multiset 13t -> 0t (helper cardDoRead, replacing a `do { ... break; } while (0)`), LimitCamVal2 58 -> 52 with multiset IDENTICAL 88/88. FindWORLDOBJ is the sharpest case: its run-44 record had proved the branch half and the return join were a COMPENSATING PAIR -- writing `return node;` directly won the branch and lost the single `mr r3,r31` -- and under the lift both come for free, because the pair is the INLINE's return lowering while the `mr` is the outer function's own return. PART 4 -- THE TWO-STAGE RETURN MERGE (BF, independent of the lift). An inlined helper whose two exits are `return <param>` and `return <other param>` splits the value web: MWCC materialises a fresh return temp and emits TWO extra `mr`s (verbatim in adsMoveRawToCooked: ours `bge ->70 / mr r0,r4 / b ->74 / mr r0,r7 / mr r4,r0` against the target's `bge ->6c / b ->70 / mr r4,r7`). Writing the second exit as an ASSIGNMENT TO THE PARAMETER followed by a return of that parameter -- `available = space; return available;` instead of `return space;` -- coalesces the return web with the caller's variable and the three `mr`s collapse to the target's one. That single edit took adsMoveRawToCooked from 175/173 insns with 2 residual `mr` to real 0, fuzzy 100.0000%. PART 5 -- PRECONDITION, measured: a `#pragma dont_inline on` covering the CALL SITE defeats the entire cure. adstream.c bracketed adsMoveRawToCooked in one and the two helpers were emitted as `bl` (real 74 against a 165/173 count gap) until the pragma was removed. GREP THE PRAGMA BRACKET BEFORE PROBING. PART 6 -- THE COST CLAUSES. (a) TAIL-MERGE: the number of exits returning the SAME value decides whether MWCC merges them. AudioEnterNextStage measured both directions on one function -- a helper with TWO early `return 0;` sites emitted TWO zero materialisations and lost count parity (real 15, T50/O51, `O[7:10]@1c-28=['bge','li','b']` against `T[7:8]@1c-20=['blt']`), while the same helper with ONE trailing `return 0;` emitted the target's single shared `li r3,0` and closed exact. (b) STORAGE CLASS AND THE DATA COST -- CONDITIONAL, AND THE CONDITION IS UNKNOWN. v2 clause (b) asserted that a bare `static` helper costs matched Data: AudioEnterNextStage measured a standalone emitted body whose exception record took ninja PROGRESS Data 177572 -> 177428 (Game Code Data 66.06% -> 65.92%), invisible to real, --ops, regnorm, the multiset and fuzzy, every one of which scored that keep as a clean win. BF's adsMoveRawToCooked record measures the OPPOSITE for two BARE `static` helpers on the same day: `fndiff --clean` reported both ONLY-IN-BASE, dead-stripped after inlining, and Data ROSE 177572 -> 177608 (Game Data 66.06% -> 66.10%). Both cannot be unconditional and neither record names the condition, so v3 does not invent one. NEW, measured at 05b3e534a with zero builds: all four helper names (adsBlockDivisor, adsLimitAvailable, CritterMoveColNode, cardDoRead) are ABSENT from `objdump -t` of their own objects and from config/GUNE5D/symbols.txt, and their units' exception tables are intact or better than the surrounding image (adstream extab 144/144 and total matched data 359/360; cardutil extab 141/144). That measurement does NOT settle the dispute, because the tree at c621fcbac spells all four `static inline` while BF's own `probed_form` records them as bare `static` -- the bare-static state is no longer reachable from HEAD. THE DECISION PROCEDURE, which costs zero builds and is what a lane should actually run: after the lift, look for the helper's name in `objdump -t` of our object. Present = a standalone body was emitted and its exception record is a Data liability; absent = it was inlined away and there is nothing to pay for. Then confirm with `defake_gate.py check <unit>`, whose DATA-CHANGED row prices the change in matched bytes since run-46 item 3 (a NEGATIVE net is a regression however good every .text arbiter looks -- claim.law.WS_frame-widening-silently-breaks-the-tus-extab-match; 46 units in the image currently lose 1866 B of exception-table bytes, so this is not a rare failure mode). DEFAULT: write `static inline`, which is what every one of the four closure sites carries in the tree today and what suppresses the standalone body by construction. Use bare `static` only with the symbol check and the DATA delta shown. (c) The lift ORPHANS the outer function's locals and MWCC keeps nominal frame space for them: CritterMoveSetup sat at multiset-IDENTICAL 77/77 with five IMMEDIATE rows that were ALL frame words (frame 32 vs 48) until `void *node; void *candidate; s32 nodeIndex;` were deleted, per claim.law.dead-nominal-local-area-tracks-declaration-count.20260831.v1. Delete them in the same edit. PART 7 -- WHERE THE CURE COSTS MORE THAN IT PAYS, so this is not read as unconditional. When the caller's destination is not the inline's return register the lift buys the branch and pays a copy: CritterAnimate (game/enemy/critter) closes the pair exactly (target-only opcodes -> none) and pays `addi r5,r3,0`, real 38 -> 108, FRESH fuzzy 98.8564 -> 98.7766; get_vmu_directory (game/sys/memcard) closes the pair and pays `li r0,1` + `mr. r30,r0` because the returned value is a live CONSTANT the inline rematerialises, fuzzy 92.7155 -> 92.1983. Both reverted on the fuzzy arbiter, and two further spellings on CritterAnimate (chained `nextIndex = candidate = helper(c)`, hoisting the helper's local) were NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL, so the result-register class is not reachable by declaration spelling. BEFORE LIFTING, check in the aligned view that the target's join register is the destination VARIABLE's register and not the ABI return register r3. PART 8 -- RANKING THE QUEUE, NEW. `nm_branchpair_census.py diff` now prints a profitability column, `profit = (target_insns - our_insns) - (target_sites - our_sites)`, the part of the count residual the pairs do not explain. Measured at d9d4c9ae7 over the live 41-row queue with the opcode-MULTISET delta as arbiter: profit 0 (n=8) has a branch-only multiset delta in 4 (50%), partial(+N) (n=9) in 0 (0%), overshoot(-N) (n=22) in 1 (5%). Rank on it; it does NOT predict exact closure -- those eight profit-0 rows carry `real` 45, 65, 93, 143, 171, 171, 261 and 627.
